avenues.name: The achievement ledger
avenues.thesis: A 296-row, event-anchored, per-row-verified corpus of US and Chinese achievements 1926–2026; 292 rows ESTABLISHED under a published promotion standard. The full 1926–2025 chronological corpus is processed, plus author-proposed per-row passes (batch 11: physical-manufacturing and 2023–2025 achievements; batch 12: maritime and defense-industrial; batch 13: the national-security view; batch 14: two US venture-capital / small-business-R&D rows anchoring Figure V) adding rows on both sides — each through the same ritual. Rows also carry a country-blind natsec / dual-use tag (Amendment 5) driving Figure III.

avenues.name: Coverage shape
avenues.thesis: Facts about the corpus under the published selection rule: US coverage is steady and invention/deployment-heavy; China's is thin early, rises late, and is completion/milestone-heavy. A statement about the ledger — NOT a momentum verdict about the world.

avenues.name: The momentum index
avenues.thesis: Now computed and shown as a constructed index (Option C gate: ESTABLISHED rows only, non-ESTABLISHED rows excluded and named). Primary = baseline equal weighting; bands span four published weightings; whiskers show the excluded non-ESTABLISHED rows (1946–1955 and 2016–2025). Re-weightable, rubric published — true only within its scope, never a measured verdict.

avenues.name: Early-century China floor
avenues.thesis: 1926–1945 China coverage is a floor, not a fact — real historical thinness compounded by English-language source bias. Posted as an open challenge: readers who know this literature can raise it, for named credit.

avenues.name: Verification in progress
avenues.thesis: Live status: 292 ESTABLISHED, 1 OPEN-UNVERIFIED, 3 REPORTED. Batches 1–10 processed the full 1926–2025 corpus; a straggler sweep resolved leftovers; batch 11 added twelve ESTABLISHED physical-manufacturing/2023–2025 rows plus one REPORTED (a Chinese EUV-lithography claim, interested-party sourced — confirmed progress is DUV not EUV); batch 12 added two ESTABLISHED China maritime rows (shipbuilding dominance; PLA Navy largest by hull count, with the mandatory US-leads-by-tonnage caveat); batch 13 added USS Gerald R. Ford and eight further defense rows (four US, four China) plus one REPORTED (the 2021 hypersonic test — independent FT report recorded alongside China's spacecraft denial), and a country-blind natsec/dual-use tag across the corpus (Figure III); batch 14 added two US rows — American Research and Development (1946, the first modern venture-capital firm) and the SBIR program (1982) — so every founder-regime tick in Figure V now anchors to a ledger row. Announced or not-yet-operational items (DF-17 parade reveal, US hypersonic weapons, Linglong-One SMR, second-gen batteries, Kimi K3, Columbia-class SSBN, AUKUS transfers) were held, not filed. Just ONE row stays open: the Chengdu–Chongqing Railway (CN-1952-1). The 2026 window is also not yet closed.

checks._comment: Single source of truth for the consistency-check RULES. Both index.html's console and verification/verify_numbers.py read these, so a threshold can never drift between the page and the verifier. Change a rule HERE and both sides enforce it on next run. (The check LOGIC is still written in each language — see AUTHORING.md — but the rules it enforces live only here.)
